ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: <image>If $R T=16, Q P=24,$ and $S T=9,$ find $P S$
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the diagram is a large triangle QPS, P and S are at the two ends of the base, and Q is above; point T is located on the base PS, and point R is located on side QS; segment RT connects T and R. In the diagram, QP and RT have the same arrow markings, indicating that RT is parallel to QP. Reasoning: Because RT ∥ QP, triangle RST and triangle QPS are similar by AA: they share the angle at vertex S, and the parallel lines produce corresponding equal angles. The corresponding sides are RT corresponding to QP, and ST corresponding to PS, therefore RT/QP = ST/PS. Substitute RT=16, QP=24, ST=9, to get 16/24 = 9/PS. Solving gives PS = 9×24/16 = 13.5.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large triangle QPS with T on segment PS and R on segment QS. The arrow markings show RT is parallel to QP. From the text, use RT=16, QP=24, and ST=9. Since RT ∥ QP, triangles RST and QPS are similar by AA similarity: angle S is shared, and the angles formed with the parallel sides match. Therefore RT/QP = ST/PS. Substitute 16/24 = 9/PS and solve to get PS = 13.5.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a dilation configuration centered at S: segment RT connects the sides SQ and SP, and RT is parallel to QP, so RT is a scaled copy of QP inside triangle SQP. Let the scale factor from the large triangle SQP to the smaller triangle SRT be k. From the text, the corresponding parallel sides give k=RT/QP=16/24=2/3. The same scale applies along the base, so ST/PS=k. With ST=9, solve 9/PS=2/3, giving PS=13.5.
